pairs.ask: Weekly Encrypted Backup Of Every Repo: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Mirror every WebermanApps repo weekly to an encrypted backup outside GitHub, such as Dropbox or an offline drive. Who does it: Security.

optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: If GitHub deletes a repo or a login is taken over, there is no copy of the code outside GitHub.

pairs.ask: Print Recovery Codes And Keep Them In A Safe: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Print the GitHub, Google and Stripe recovery codes and keep them offline in a safe. Never store them on the shared computer. Who does it: You.

Never store them on the</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">shared computer. Who does it: You.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: If a key or phone is lost without recovery codes, you can be locked out of your own company.

pairs.ask: Real Login For smartupkeep.ai With Cloudflare Access: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Use Cloudflare Access (free up to 50 people): one email PIN per person and a log of who signed in. You create the account and OK the nameserver change. Who does it: You, Then UpKeep.

optionA.desc: In the monthly review, restore one repo and one Dropbox file from backup and check they open. Who does it: Security.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: A backup nobody has tested may not work when you need it.

pairs.ask: Passkey On The Stripe Account: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Turn on a passkey or hardware key for Stripe before the first real payment, and add Stripe to the 2FA checklist. Who does it: You.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-height:100%;max-width:100%"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Turn on a passkey or hardware key for</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Stripe before the first real payment,</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">and add Stripe to the 2FA checklist.</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Who does it: You.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Stripe is not on the 2FA checklist yet, but it will hold member payments once smartupkeep.ai launches.

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Use only Stripe hosted Checkout or Payment Links, with the Stripe portal for billing changes. Card data never touches our pages. Who does it: UpKeep.

Who does it:</text><text x="18" y="168" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">UpKeep.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Collecting card numbers in our own forms would make us responsible for card security rules (PCI).

pairs.ask: Two Hardware Keys For Google And GitHub: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Buy two hardware keys (one main, one spare), add them plus a passkey to Google and both GitHub accounts, then turn off SMS fallback. Who does it: You.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Account takeover is the top way to lose everything. SMS codes can be stolen with a SIM swap or a fake login page.

pairs.ask: Your OK Before Agents Email, Pay Or Delete: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Agents draft; you approve emails, payments, deletions and pushes to customer sites. Internal dashboards keep publishing on their own. Who does it: All Agents.

Internal dashboards</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">keep publishing on their own. Who does</text><text x="18" y="168" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">it: All Agents.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Agents read web pages and email, and hidden instructions in that content can hijack them (prompt injection).

pairs.ask: Block Force-Push And Deletion On main: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Once each agent has its own token, add a rule on main that only blocks force-push and deletion. Publishing keeps working. Who does it: Security, With Your OK.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Right now any agent or leaked login could wipe a repo's history or delete main. Full review rules would block agents from publishing.

pairs.ask: One-Page Breach Plan For Michigan: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Legal writes who to call and a notice template. Security writes the steps to revoke keys and lock accounts. Who does it: Legal And Security.

Who</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">does it: Legal And Security.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Michigan law (MCL 445.72) requires notifying affected residents after certain breaches, and there is no plan yet.

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Yes retires it now: UpKeep removes it from both gates and u9 and the other codes keep working. No keeps it until the Cloudflare cutover as planned. Who does it: UpKeep, With Your OK.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: At your request, UpKeep kept the old launch-day password working alongside u9 on smartupkeep.ai and the review build until the Cloudflare cutover. Old passwords also sit in plain text in git history, so anyone with the repo history can read it.

pairs.ask: Cyber Insurance Quotes For Smart Upkeep LLC: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Legal gets quotes for cyber liability, general liability and professional (E&O) cover, and you choose a budget. Who does it: Legal, Then You.

pairs.ask: Collect Only Name, Email, Address And Phone From Members: Do It Or Not Now?

pairs.ask: Privacy Policy Before Member Data: Do It Or Not Now?

pairs.ask: Retire The Shared GitHub Login After Tokens Work: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: When every agent's token passes its publish test, sign the shared login out of the box. Who does it: Security, With Your OK.

Who does it: Security,</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">With Your OK.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: The broad login stays active until every agent has its own token, so the risk stays until it is removed.

pairs.ask: Monthly Check Of The GitHub Security Log: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Add a GitHub security log review and a collaborator list check to the monthly review. Who does it: Security.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-height:100%;max-width:100%"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Add a GitHub security log review and a</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">collaborator list check to the monthly</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">review. Who does it: Security.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Without a look at the log, a strange login or token use by an agent could go unnoticed.

Why it matters:</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Without a look at the log, a strange</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">login or token use by an agent could</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">go unnoticed.</text></svg>

pairs.ask: One Expiring Token Per Agent: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: You create one fine-grained token per agent, limited to its own repos and expiring within 90 days. Security sets them up and tests each one. Who does it: You, Then Security.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-height:100%;max-width:100%"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">You create one fine-grained token per</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">agent, limited to its own repos and</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">expiring within 90 days. Security sets</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">them up and tests each one. Who does</text><text x="18" y="168" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">it: You, Then Security.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: All agents share one broad GitHub login on the shared computer. That login works like a master key to every repo.
